metadata.name: CSV Plotter
metadata.description: Read a CSV, reshape it into plot-ready points with a code node, and chart it. No AI and no network: this one runs anywhere the engine runs. Paths are relative to the working directory, so run this from the repository root.

nodes.label: CSV
nodes.description: Prompts for the file when the graph runs; Enter keeps the default.

config.code_prompt: Turn the CSV into a list of {label, value} points, largest first, scaled to millions.
config.code:
import csv
import io


def run(inputs):
    """CSV text -> plot-ready points.

    The chart is drawn by the app, so this only reshapes data: a list of
    {"label": str, "value": number}. Column names are read from the header
    rather than hard-coded, so the same node plots any two-column CSV.
    """
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(inputs.get("content") or "")))
    if not rows:
        return {"points": []}

    columns = list(rows[0].keys())
    label_column = columns[0]
    value_column = columns[1] if len(columns) > 1 else columns[0]

    points = []
    for row in rows:
        raw = str(row.get(value_column) or "").strip().replace(" ", "").replace(".", "")
        raw = raw.replace(",", ".")
        try:
            value = float(raw)
        except ValueError:
            continue  # a stray footer line is not a data point
        points.append({"label": str(row.get(label_column) or ""), "value": round(value / 1_000_000, 1)})

    points.sort(key=lambda point: point["value"], reverse=True)
    return {"points": points}
